title: Can an Internal Parameter Be Used to Effectively Regularize MVDR Weights?
content: The Minimum Variance Distortionless Response (MVDR) beamformer offers optimal spatial selectivity but suffers from severe numerical instability in non-stationary acoustic environments. Target encroachment, steering vector mismatch, and finite-snapshot variance cause the spatial covariance matrix (SCM) to become acutely ill-conditioned. As the matrix approaches singularity, the norm of the inverted SCM diverges, leading to unbounded filter weights and a catastrophic collapse in White Noise Gain (WNG). While trace-relative diagonal loading mitigates this instability, utilizing a fixed regularization parameter forces an intractable compromise between spatial selectivity and numerical robustness. This paper proposes a spatially informed, time-frequency adaptive regularization framework for MVDR beamformers. We derive an orthogonal subspace leakage metric that quantifies the projection error between the assumed target steering vector and the dominant spatial subspace of the recursively estimated mixture SCM. This metric serves as a computationally efficient, instantaneous proxy for spatial difficulty. By mapping this leakage through a continuous logistic sigmoid clutch bounded by an empirically validated, array-scaled transition point (1/M), the proposed method continuously adapts the trace-relative loading. Quantitative evaluations across varying array geometries demonstrate that this continuous mapping reduces frame-to-frame filter weight jitter by an order of magnitude compared to binary thresholding. The proposed architecture autonomously navigates the feasible performance frontier, bounding WNG collapse during spatial degradation while preserving maximum selectivity in favorable geometries, all without requiring environment-specific threshold tuning or iterative convex solvers.
